results.content:
DevPit fixes this with a dedicated design-qa step. After the coder finishes, design-qa takes over. It screenshots affected pages at multiple viewports using Playwright, reads the screenshots (Claude is multimodal, it can see images), and audits everything: layout, responsive behavior, typography, accessibility. If something looks wrong, it reports exactly what’s broken, and DevPit loops back to the coder to fix it.

For mobile projects, the same thing works with Maestro and simulator screenshots. iOS Simulator or Android Emulator.

This changed how much I trust the output. Before, I’d have to pull up the browser after every change and eyeball it myself. Now there’s a dedicated agent whose only job is to look at what was built and find visual problems.

## It’s Not Just Claude [...] What I love about this is that each step is visible. I can peek at any agent, see exactly what it’s doing, and understand why it made the choices it did. When something goes wrong, I know _which_ agent failed and _what_ context it had. The dashboard shows me the full history of every run.

This is fundamentally different from a single Claude session where you have to scroll back through hundreds of messages to figure out when things went sideways.

## Try It

If you’ve been using AI coding agents without orchestration, you’re running a team where everyone talks over each other in the same room. DevPit gives each specialist their own office, their own brief, and a clean handoff protocol. [...] Sitemap

Open in app

Sign up

Sign in

 work in a real terminal. You see every file it reads, every edit it makes, every command it runs. If something looks wrong, you see it happening, not after the fact in a log.

The TUI dashboard makes this even easier. Run `dp` with no arguments and you get an interactive view of all your pipeline runs. Running, passed, failed, with the ability to drill into any run and see step-by-step output.

## Workflows Are Just YAML

The default pipeline (architect, coder, tester, reviewer, design-qa) works great out of the box. But every project is different. DevPit lets you define custom workflows in YAML:

results.content:
Title: [FEATURE] Make the mobile Code tab a native client for agent-view background sessions · Issue #65972 · anthropics/claude-code · GitHub
You signed in with another tab or window. # [FEATURE] Make the mobile Code tab a native client for agent-view background sessions #65972. [[FEATURE] Make the mobile Code tab a native client for agent-view background sessions](/anthropics/claude-code/issues/65972#top)#65972. The nearest, [[FEATURE] Add SSH and/or Mosh connectivity to the Claude Code mobile app #57543](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/57543), asks for SSH/Mosh to the mobile app (a *better terminal*); this asks for the opposite — a native client with **no terminal involved**. `claude agents` (agent view) is the best multi-session experience in Claude Code: a multiplexed view of persistent background conversations, supervisor-managed, grouped by Working / Needs input / Ready for review, surviving sleep and reattachable after restart. 1. The only way to reach these background agents from a phone today is to SSH into the host and use the agent-view TUI in a mobile terminal (e.g. Termius). 2. `claude remote-control` is native on mobile but operates a **completely separate session pool**. Sessions I started in agent view never appear there; it has no introspection into the supervisor's background agents. Net: I have a fleet of persistent agents running great on an always-on machine, and **no native, terminal-free way to check or steer them from my phone** — which is exactly when I'm away from the desk and a session goes "Needs input.". Make the native **mobile Code tab a client for the agent-view session pool** — render the *same* supervisor-managed background sessions natively, no SSH terminal in the loop. Surface could be a flag on the existing server (`claude remote-control --attach-agents`) or a "serve to mobile" toggle in agent view — design detail, not the ask. * **SSH/Mosh to the TUI ([[FEATURE] Add SSH and/or Mosh connectivity to the Claude Code mobile app #57543](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/57543))** — the workaround I use today and explicitly want to eliminate; it improves the terminal path rather than removing it. * **`claude remote-control`** — native, but a separate pool with no view of the background agents; no multiplexed manager, no reboot-reattach model. 2. On my phone, in the native Claude app's Code tab (no SSH, no terminal), I see all 6 with live status.

results.content:
Custom workflows support arbitrary step sequences, context dependencies, and configurable pass/fail markers.

## Installation

### Prerequisites

 tmux 3.0+ — agents run in tmux sessions
 An AI CLI — Claude Code (default), Gemini CLI, Codex, or others

### From source

```
cd# builds and installs to ~/.local/bin/dp #
```

### From npm

```
npm install -g devpit
```

## Quick Start

```
# 1. Create a workflow (one-time) ## 2. Run the pipeline # "Add a health check endpoint" " "
```

`dp create` spawns Claude to interview you about your project, then generates agent files (`.claude/agents/.md`) and a workflow (`.claude/workflows/default.yaml`). Use `--default` for the standard template or describe a custom workflow.

## Commands

### `dp` (no args) [...] ## Commands

### `dp` (no args)

Launch the interactive TUI dashboard. View running and past pipelines, start new runs, create workflows, and edit workflow configs — all from one interface.

### `dp pipeline "task"`

Run a workflow pipeline. Loads the default workflow from `.claude/workflows/default.yaml`, or specify a custom one with `--workflow`.

```
"Fix the login form validation" " " "Refactor auth module" " " "Optimize performance" " "
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
 --- 
| `--agent` | claude | AI runtime (claude, gemini, codex, etc.) |
| `--model` | opus[1m] | Model override |
| `--timeout` | 10m | Max time per step |
| `--retries` | 3 | Max loop-back retries |
| `--workflow` | default | Custom workflow name (from `.claude/workflows/`) |

### `dp create [prompt]` [...] Read an agent's recent terminal output.

```
dp pipeline peek coder dp pipeline peek tester -n 200
```

### `dp pipeline stop`

Stop all running pipeline agent sessions.

## TUI Dashboard

Run `dp` with no arguments to launch the interactive dashboard:

 Dashboard — view running and past pipeline runs, retry failed ones, kill active sessions
 New run (`n`) — launch a pipeline with a task, workflow, and agent selection
 Create workflow (`c`) — generate a new workflow with Claude
 Edit workflow (`e`) — modify workflow configs: reorder steps, edit fields, add/remove steps
 History (`h`) — browse past runs with status and details

## Custom Workflows

Workflows are YAML files in `.claude/workflows/`:
